# 🧩 ValueKey

**ValueKey** is a lightweight, strongly-typed identifier for entity values. It wraps an integer ID generated by
[EntityKeyStore](EntityKeyStore.md), allowing fast and type-safe access to entity values without runtime string
lookups.

## 🧩 Overview

Instead of passing string value names everywhere, you can define `ValueKey` instances once and reuse them. The key stores
the integer ID internally, so operations like `GetValue`, `SetValue`, and `AddValue` are fast and allocation-free.

```csharp
public static partial class GameContextAPI
{
    public static readonly ValueKey<IGameContext, IMultiEntityPool<GameEntityType, IGameEntity>> EntityPool =
        new(nameof(EntityPool));

    public static readonly ValueKey<IGameContext, IEntityWorld<IGameEntity>> EntityWorld =
        new(nameof(EntityWorld));

    public static readonly ValueKey<IGameContext, EntitySpawnInfo[]> InitialEntities =
        new(nameof(InitialEntities));
}
```

These keys can then be used with extension methods from `Extensions_Values.cs`:

```csharp
var pool = context.GetValue(GameContextAPI.EntityPool);
var world = context.GetValue(GameContextAPI.EntityWorld);
```

---

## 🔍 Variants

| Struct | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `ValueKey<T>` | Value key bound to a value type `T`. Can be used with any [IEntity](../Entities/IEntity.md). |
| `ValueKey<E, T>` | Value key bound to both entity type `E` and value type `T`. Prevents accidental misuse across entity types. |

---

## 🗂 Examples of Usage

### Define Value Keys in an API Class

```csharp
public static partial class GameContextAPI
{
    public static readonly ValueKey<IGameContext, IMultiEntityPool<GameEntityType, IGameEntity>> EntityPool =
        new(nameof(EntityPool));

    public static readonly ValueKey<IGameContext, IEntityWorld<IGameEntity>> EntityWorld =
        new(nameof(EntityWorld));

    public static readonly ValueKey<IGameContext, EntitySpawnInfo[]> InitialEntities =
        new(nameof(InitialEntities));
}
```

### Access Values via Extension Methods

```csharp
public static class EntityUseCase
{
    public static void SpawnInitialUnits(this IGameContext gameContext)
    {
        EntitySpawnInfo[] spawnDataSet = gameContext.GetValue(GameContextAPI.InitialEntities);
        foreach (EntitySpawnInfo spawnInfo in spawnDataSet)
        {
            GameEntityType entityType = spawnInfo.entityType;
            foreach (Vector2Int point in spawnInfo.points)
                gameContext.Spawn(entityType, point, out _, notify: false);
        }
    }

    public static bool Spawn(
        this IGameContext context,
        GameEntityType type,
        Vector2Int position,
        out IGameEntity entity,
        bool notify = true
    )
    {
        entity = null;

        GameEntityBoard entityBoard = context.GetValue(GameContextAPI.GameBoard);
        if (!entityBoard.IsFreePosition(position))
            return false;

        IMultiEntityPool<GameEntityType, IGameEntity> pool = context.GetValue(GameContextAPI.EntityPool);
        entity = pool.Rent(type);

        IEntityWorld<IGameEntity> entityWorld = context.GetValue(GameContextAPI.EntityWorld);
        entityWorld.Add(entity);

        return true;
    }
}
```

### Direct Use

```csharp
IEntity entity = ...;

entity.AddValue(GameContextAPI.EntityWorld, world);
var world = entity.GetValue(GameContextAPI.EntityWorld);
```

## 🔍 API Reference

### ValueKey\<T\>

```csharp
public readonly struct ValueKey<T> : IEquatable<ValueKey<T>>
```

Strongly typed to the value type `T`.

#### `ValueKey(string)`

```csharp
public ValueKey(string name)
```

- **Description:** Creates a value key from a string name.
- **Parameter:** `name` — The value name.

#### `ValueKey(int)`

```csharp
public ValueKey(int id)
```

- **Description:** Creates a value key from an existing integer ID.
- **Parameter:** `id` — The numeric value identifier.

#### `ToString()`

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

- **Description:** Returns the original value name via [EntityKeyStore.IdToName](EntityKeyStore.md).

### ValueKey\<E, T\>

```csharp
public readonly struct ValueKey<E, T> : IEquatable<ValueKey<E, T>> where E : IEntity
```

Bound to both entity type `E` and value type `T`.

Same API as `ValueKey<T>`, but the entity type parameter provides additional compile-time safety.

---

## 📌 Best Practices

- Define value keys once in a static API class and reuse them.
- Use `ValueKey<E, T>` when multiple entity types exist in the same project.
- Prefer keys over string names in hot paths to avoid repeated `EntityKeyStore.NameToId` lookups.
- Keep value names stable — changing a name changes the generated ID unless a deterministic algorithm is used.
- Use `TryGetValue` when a value may not be present to avoid exceptions.
